analysis.title: Nextdoor Holdings (NXDR) Q3'26 Earnings Review: User Growth Continues Reacceleration; Monetization & Product Execution Remain Key Areas of Focus
key_insights: Q3'26 Platform WAUs reached a record 24.5mn (+14% YoY, +7% QoQ per management commentary; the positives section cites +13% YoY). Weekly contributors grew +27% YoY and +12% QoQ. Management says growth is organic and product-led.
Q3 revenue of $79mm beat GS ($77mm) and consensus ($77mm) and the $76-78mm guide. Adj. EBITDA of $10mm beat GS and consensus ($8mm each) and the $6.5-8.0mm guide, at a 13.1% margin.

Self-serve revenue grew +35% YoY and is now 69% of revenue. Management pointed to new ad products, including Neighborhood Intelligence and Opportunity Alerts, as incremental monetization vectors into 2027.

Q3 ARPU was $3.22, below GS ($3.35) and down 1% QoQ. Q4 ARPU growth is expected to moderate to +1% YoY and decline sequentially. Management attributes this to reactivated users, who monetize at lower levels at first and improve over time.
Q4 Adj. EBITDA guide of $10-11mm is below GS and Street estimates. Management said the Q3 Adj. EBITDA beat was helped partly by expense timing.
Management commentary implies Q4 WAUs roughly flat sequentially, in line with typical seasonality, after three quarters of sequential growth.

Management says Nextdoor benefits from AI/ML tailwinds given its first-party data, local intent and user-generated content. It is building agentic experiences, with Ask now integrated into search for US users.
Capital allocation priorities are balanced investment and returning capital to shareholders. GS models share repurchases of $43mm in 2026 and $30mm a year in 2027 and 2028.
GS maintains Neutral and cuts its 12-month PT to $3.00 from $3.25 on lower forward operating estimates and management commentary. The PT implies 41.5% upside from $2.12.

The PT is an equal blend of 2.0x EV/Sales on NTM+1 year estimates and a modified DCF using 25.0x EV/GAAP EBITDA (cut from 35.0x) on NTM+4 year estimates. The multiple reduction reflects the SMID-cap digital ad peer group's 3-year historical average of 25.0x.
Scenario values are $1.50 downside (-28%), $3.00 base and $3.75 upside (+79%).

market_movers.rationale: Neutral maintained, PT cut from $3.25 to $3.00. The DCF multiple fell to 25.0x from 35.0x, and Q4 Adj. EBITDA guidance and ARPU came in softer than expected despite the Q3 beat.

earnings_insights: NXDR Q3'26 reported (6 Nov 2026 note): revenue $79mm vs GS $77mm and consensus $77mm, guide $76-78mm, +14% YoY.
NXDR Q3'26 reported Adj. EBITDA $10mm (13.1% margin) vs GS $8mm and consensus $8mm, guide $6.5-8.0mm. Management said expense timing helped the beat.
NXDR Q3'26 reported GAAP EBITDA of $(4)mm (-4.9% margin) vs GS $(8)mm and consensus $(7)mm.
NXDR Q3'26 reported ARPU $3.22 vs GS estimate $3.35, -1% QoQ and +1% YoY. Platform WAUs 24.5mm vs GS estimate 23.1mm.

NXDR Q4'26 company guide: revenue $78-90mm per GS table and Adj. EBITDA $10-11mm, below GS and Street. GS Q4 estimate: revenue $79mm (unchanged), Adj. EBITDA $11mm (from $12mm), GAAP EPS $(0.00) (from $(0.01)), Adj. EPS $0.03 (from $0.04).

GS FY2026 estimates: revenue $294mm, Adj. EBITDA $31mm, Adj. EPS $0.10. FY2027 estimates: revenue $331mm (unchanged), Adj. EBITDA $51mm (unchanged), GAAP EPS $0.00 (from $0.01), Adj. EPS $0.14. FY2028 estimates: revenue $370mm, Adj. EBITDA $74mm, Adj. EPS $0.19.
GS cuts annualized ARPU estimates: FY2026 to $12.95 (from $13.23), FY2027 to $13.21 (from $13.85), FY2028 to $14.07 (from $14.80). WAU estimates rise 5% in each period.
risk_factors: User growth could deviate from modeling assumptions through new cohorts, international expansion or engagement.
International revenue trajectory could differ given go-to-market investments and ad product innovation.
Execution on monetization: advertiser scale and depth, new ad formats, and targeting, measurement and attribution improvements.
Competition for users and ad spend from other social and digital media platforms.
Increased regulatory scrutiny of media platforms on user data, privacy and content moderation.
Exposure to macro volatility and investor risk appetite for growth stocks.
The Q3 Adj. EBITDA beat was partly from expense timing, and reactivated users may weigh on ARPU near term.

tension_points.bull_case: Platform WAUs hit a record 24.5mn, weekly contributors rose +27% YoY and self-serve revenue rose +35% YoY. New ad products such as Neighborhood Intelligence and Opportunity Alerts are expected to support monetization into 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Q4 ARPU growth slows to +1% YoY and declines sequentially as reactivated users monetize at lower levels. Q4 Adj. EBITDA guidance is below the Street, the Q3 beat was helped by expense timing, and Q4 WAUs are expected to be roughly flat sequentially.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bull case weakens if ARPU does not improve as reactivated users mature, or if newer ad products fail to turn higher engagement into incremental revenue growth.

theme_stances.key_argument: User growth is accelerating, but monetization and ad product execution decide how durable the operating trajectory is.
theme_stances.evidence: execution against the company’s expanding product roadmap key
